big: A rule of thumb: corpus ≈ 25 times first-year expenses, which is a 4% withdrawal. In the lesson's example, first-year expenses are about ₹30.9 lakh. That points to about ₹7.7 crore. But many planners use 3 to 3.5% for India.

lines: It is a starting point. With India's higher inflation and returns, many planners use a lower rate such as 3 to 3.5% for safety. At 3.5%, the same example needs about ₹8.8 crore. Then work back to the monthly SIP. These are planning aids, not guarantees, so review every year.
